title: Demurrage and Detention Free Time: Amount of the Final Demurrage Line
content:
## Definition of the amount

The amount of a Demurrage and Detention Free Time record's final demurrage line is the total of the day rates of every demurrage day it bills, each rate being the one for that day's slab and rate class after any dangerous-goods uplift has been applied to it. That total is rounded to the cent once, as a whole; no day rate is rounded separately.

Stated at the level of the slab groups, the unrounded amount is: the slab 1 days multiplied by the slab 1 demurrage rate, together with the slab 2 days multiplied by the slab 2 rate, the slab 3 days multiplied by the slab 3 rate and the slab 4 days multiplied by the slab 4 rate, the whole then increased by the applicable uplift percentage of itself, or by nothing where no uplift applies. Because the same percentage lifts every demurrage day rate, raising the total by it gives the same figure as raising each day rate.

## Worked illustration (hypothetical rates and uplift)

Rates of 70.00, 115.00, 162.00 and 214.00 for slabs 1 to 4; 3 days in slab 2 and 2 days in slab 3; a dangerous-goods booking under an assumed uplift of 30 percent.

| Part | Figure |
|---|---|
| slab 2 days: 3 at 115.00 | 345.00 |
| slab 3 days: 2 at 162.00 | 324.00 |
| unrounded amount before uplift | 669.00 |
| uplift of 30 percent of 669.00 | 200.70 |
| line amount | 869.70 |

Without the dangerous-goods cargo type the same line would amount to 669.00.
